result.summary: Ignores the `addrMe` address received in `version` messages from privacy network peers like Tor and I2P. This prevents nodes from recording or self-advertising a peer-provided routable IP address over an anonymous connection.
result.problem: When connecting out to privacy network peers, those peers should not know our IP address, yet a malicious Tor or I2P peer can report an arbitrary routable IP in the `addrMe` field of their `version` message. If processed, the local node may self-advertise that address paired with its custom listening port, creating an identity fingerprint that correlates its clearnet and privacy network activity.
evidence: PR description: 'this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions: 1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman 2. we need to be using a unique enough port.'

Commit fb178b2374: 'if we don't ignore it, we can end up sending them as self advertisement the routable ipv4 address they sent us and our listening port. ignoring it will help prevent our custom clearnet port leaks to privacy networks.'
result.scope_notes: Small patch touching version message processing in net_processing and adding an accompanying test.
result.card: Bitcoin Core nodes ignore the addrMe field in version messages from Tor and I2P peers. Malicious privacy network peers can currently return a routable IP address that the node may subsequently self-advertise alongside its listening port, risking correlation of a node's clearnet and privacy network identities. The PR description notes this fingerprint was identified by researchers and requires outbound connection to the adversary and non-default port usage to exploit.

risk.why: Mistakes in processing P2P version messages or network address handling could break outbound connection establishment or valid address discovery.
